title: Aurum Alpha RBAC model
description: The shapes of standards/070-rbac.md: permission, scope, role, condition and grant. This file fixes the model; contracts/rbac/decisions.json fixes the behaviour. schemaVersion 1 — evolves additively per PC6.

permission.description: resource.action, lowercase, snake_case within segments, exactly two segments (RB2). The dot is reserved for permissions and the colon for scopes so no identifier is ambiguous. Three segments are forbidden: system.dashboard.view is system_dashboard.view, which keeps the check an equality rather than a prefix question.

scope.description: Either the literal 'global' or a type:id pair such as tenant:acme (RB5). The application declares which scope types exist and how they contain one another; this contract fixes the shape and leaves the hierarchy to the application, because a standard naming the levels would fit no two products.

conditionOperator.description: The closed operator set of RB11, fixed by the standard; no product adds one. equals_subject: the property is the caller's id. contains_subject: the caller's id is in the property, a set. within: the property is a timestamp no older than the role entry's duration before now. A property that is empty fails every operator.

condition.description: A condition declared in code on one resource (RB11), as RB1 declares a permission. It names one property of that resource's object and one operator. It is known as resource.name, such as lead.owner, and a role entry on a permission of that resource names it by name alone.

resource.description: The resource segment of the permissions this condition can restrict (RB2): the object the act is done to.

name.description: How a role entry and the identity document name the condition.

property.description: The property of the object the condition reads. The query that fetches the object selects it.

conditionReference.description: A condition named in a role entry: its name, or its name with a parameter. within takes exactly one parameter, an ISO 8601 duration such as P5D, and the other operators take none. Whether a parameter fits its operator is validated when the role is written (RB3), since the operator is the declaration's.

conditionGroups.description: Any-of groups of all-of conditions (RB11): the entry holds for an object when every condition in at least one group holds. There is no NOT, no nesting and no expression.

role.description: A named set of permissions (RB3). Roles do not nest and do not inherit — a role that should have what another has lists the same permissions, so that what a person can do stays readable from the role's own definition. A permission is held once, either unconditionally or with the condition groups 'conditions' gives it.

name.description: Stable identifier. Display names are the application's own concern.

permissions.description: Every entry MUST be in the application's declared permission set (RB1), validated at write time. A stored role carrying a typo grants nothing and says nothing.

conditions.description: The role's conditional entries, by permission (RB3, RB11). Optional: a permission with no key here is held unconditionally, and a role without the member is unconditional throughout. Validated at write time: every key is a permission in this role's 'permissions', every condition is declared on that permission's resource, and every parameter fits its operator. A role listing a permission twice is refused.

grant.description: Binds a subject to a role within a scope (RB5). A session acts in one grant, and the effective permission set is that grant's role's set: grants are never combined and there are no negative grants.

subject.description: The application's own user or service-account id, per IP1. Never the identity provider's subject.

decision.description: What check() returns (RB8). Never a bare boolean: a denial that cannot say why is the SC2 reason-giving failure on the surface where it matters most. An allowance names the grant that satisfied it; a denial names one of the eight reasons. Both are logged and shown to an administrator; neither reaches an unauthorised caller, whose response is the HA3 envelope.

reason.description: Which grant satisfied the check. Present when allowed is true and absent otherwise: there is no satisfying grant to name.

denial.description: Why the check was refused, one of the eight reasons RB8 names. Present when allowed is false and absent otherwise. undeclared_permission and invalid_scope are also errors; the decision beside the error carries them.
